body.heading: Helping is a superpower you already have
paragraphs: You do not need to be big to be helpful. Homes and classrooms run on hundreds of tiny jobs — and most of them are exactly child-sized. Helping is not about being perfect at a job; it is about noticing that a job needs doing.
Here are ten real ways to help, starting today.

body.heading: Helping at home
paragraphs: Carry something: a bag, a book, a basket of laundry. Your arms are strong enough for something.
Water a plant. Plants cannot ask, so noticing they are thirsty is a kind of listening.
Set the table, or clear your own plate after a meal. Future-you says thank you.
Tidy one small corner — a shoe pile, a toy box, your own backpack.

body.heading: Helping at school
paragraphs: Hold the door for the person behind you. It takes two seconds and changes their morning.
Help a classmate find a lost crayon, book or mitten. Two searchers are faster than one.
If someone drops their things, kneel down and help pick them up. Everyone has dropped everything before.
Thank the people who help your school — the cooks, the cleaners, the crossing guard — by name if you know it.

body.heading: Helping with your heart
paragraphs: Notice someone sitting alone and invite them to join. This is the bravest helping of all.
Draw a picture or write a note for someone who is sad, sick or far away.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Which helping job from this chart will you do TODAY? Tell someone your plan — plans told out loud happen more often.
2. Think of a helper in your life who is easy to forget (the bus driver? the mail carrier?). How could you thank them this week?

takeaway: Helping is noticing plus doing: carry, water, tidy, hold the door, include someone — small jobs that genuinely hold a home and a school together.
